name.text: Types of Functions — identifying degree from a disguised expression

questiontext.text:
Consider the expression, written in a slightly unusual form:

\[ y = {@displayexpr@}. \]

Once fully expanded, what type of function is this?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Expanding fully: \( {@displayexpr@} = {@degexpr@} \).

The highest power of \(x\) that appears (the degree) tells you the type: degree 1 is linear, degree 2 is quadratic, degree 3 is cubic. Here the degree is {@deg@}, so this is {@ftype_opt@}.

Don't judge the type from how the expression looks before expanding — a product of factors can hide a lower (or higher) degree than you might expect, and terms can cancel.
